message.content: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","agent_id":"researcher","description":"Conduct web research on competing EV charging connector standards (at minimum: CCS1/CCS2, CHAdeMO, NACS/Tesla, GB/T, Type 2/Type 1). For each standard gather: typical power ranges (AC and DC), max charging speeds, regional adoption and regulatory status, vehicle compatibility, common use-cases (public fast chargers, depot/fleet chargers, on-board charger limits), installation and equipment cost drivers, interoperability or adapter availability, major manufacturers/operators supporting it, and recent market/standardization trends or transition risks. Provide concise summaries for each connector, list all source links, and finish with 3 short, actionable implications for a fleet buyer (charging uptime, future-proofing, and procurement/installation considerations). Save results as a single Markdown file.","dependencies":[],"produces":"ev_connector_research.md","consumes":[],"rationale":"Researcher has web_search and is best suited to collect authoritative, current sources.","needs_tools":["web_search"]},{"id":"s2","agent_id":"creative","description":"Using ev_connector_research.md, write a one-page (approx. 400–600 words) Markdown comparison tailored for a fleet buyer. Include: a brief executive summary with a clear recommendation, a compact side-by-side comparison (pros/cons and suitability by fleet type and region), operational impacts (charging speed, uptime, adapters, maintenance), rough cost/installation considerations, and a 5-item procurement checklist. Cite the sources from the research file. Save the output as a Markdown file optimized for direct sharing with procurement stakeholders.","dependencies":["s1"],"produces":"one_page_comparison.md","consumes":["ev_connector_research.md"],"rationale":"Creative writes clear, audience-tailored one-page reports and can produce a polished Markdown deliverable.","needs_tools":["read_file","write_file"]}]}
